models.name: hrms_members
models.description:
Registered member accounts with email/password credentials and global profile information.

This table serves as the primary actor identity for authenticated users in the system. Each member has a unique email address and password hash for authentication. The member record contains a global profile (display name, avatar, phone number) that is shared across all organizations the user belongs to.

Key relationships:
- {@link hrms_organization_members} — One member can have multiple organization memberships across different organizations
- {@link hrms_member_sessions} — One member can have multiple active sessions for tracking logins
- {@link hrms_member_password_resets} — One member can have multiple password reset requests (expired tokens)
- {@link hrms_member_email_verifications} — One member can have multiple email verification requests
- {@link hrms_employees} — One member may be linked to an employee record in organizations they belong to
- {@link hrms_activity_logs} — One member can perform many actions logged in activity logs (via performed_by_id reference)

Behavioral notes:
- Email must be unique across all members
- Members can belong to multiple organizations simultaneously
- Members can have multiple sessions active at once (different devices/browsers)
- Soft delete via deleted_at for account deletion workflow
- Password hash is never stored in plaintext

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Unique email address used for authentication. Must be unique across all members.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: BCrypt or similar hashed password. Never stored in plaintext.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: User's display name shown across the platform. Used for identification in activity logs and member lists.

plainFields.name: avatar_uri
plainFields.description: URL to the user's avatar image. Optional profile customization.

plainFields.name: phone_number
plainFields.description: User's phone number. Optional contact information.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the member account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the member record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the member account was soft-deleted. NULL means active.

models.name: hrms_member_sessions
models.description:
JWT session tokens with access and refresh tokens for member authentication. Tracks member login sessions with organization context switching capability.

Each session stores the JWT access token and refresh token used for API authentication, along with connection metadata (IP address, referrer URL, current page URL) and the organization context selected by the member. Members can have multiple active sessions (different devices or browsers) and can switch between organizations without logging out.

Sessions are automatically expired based on expiration timestamps. Members can also manually terminate specific sessions through logout operations. This table is a child entity of the {@link hrms_members} actor table and supports many-to-one relationship (one member, many sessions).

foreignFields.name: hrms_member_id
foreignFields.description: Referenced member's {@link hrms_members.id}. Belongs to the member actor who initiated this session.

foreignFields.name: current_organization_id
foreignFields.description: Currently selected organization context for this session. When null, the member has not selected an organization yet.

plainFields.name: access_token
plainFields.description: JWT access token for API authentication. This token is sent with each API request for authorization.

plainFields.name: refresh_token
plainFields.description: JWT refresh token for renewing expired access tokens. Used when the access token expires but the session is still valid.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: Client IP address from which the session was initiated. Used for security auditing and detecting suspicious access patterns.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Page URL where the member was logged in from. Provides context about the navigation path during login.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL from the HTTP request during login. Useful for analytics and security auditing.

plainFields.name: user_agent
plainFields.description: Browser and device user agent string. Used for identifying the client device and browser type.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Session creation timestamp when the member successfully logged in.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Session expiration timestamp. Sessions are invalidated when current time exceeds this value.

models.name: hrms_member_password_resets
models.description:
Password reset tokens for member account recovery.

This table captures all password reset requests made by members, providing an audit trail for account recovery attempts. Each record contains a unique reset token with expiration timestamp and usage status.

Key relationships:
- Belongs to {@link hrms_members} via hrms_member_id (member who requested the reset)
- The token is sent to the member's email for verification
- Tokens are one-time use and expire after a set duration

Business rules:
- Each reset token is unique and can only be used once
- Tokens automatically expire after the expiration time
- Used tokens are marked with used_at timestamp for audit purposes
- Members can have multiple pending reset tokens (only the newest is typically used)
- This table serves as an audit trail for security and compliance

Note: Email address is accessed via {@link hrms_members} FK reference; storing email separately would violate 3NF normalization.

foreignFields.name: hrms_member_id
foreignFields.description: Member's {@link hrms_members.id} who requested the password reset.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Unique reset token sent to member's email for verification.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Expiration timestamp when the reset token becomes invalid.

plainFields.name: used_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the token was successfully used to reset password (nullable if not yet used).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Creation timestamp of the password reset request.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update timestamp (updated when token is used).

models.name: hrms_member_email_verifications
models.description:
Email verification tokens for member registration validation.

This table stores one-time use verification tokens sent to members' email addresses during account registration. Each verification token is unique, time-limited, and marked as used once the email is confirmed.

Key relationships:
- Belongs to a single {@link hrms_members} member account
- Multiple verification attempts can exist for the same member (e.g., resend verification)
- Tokens are single-use and expire after a set period

Behavioral notes:
- Only one active (unused, not expired) verification token should exist per member at a time
- Used tokens are retained for audit purposes but marked with deleted_at
- Token generation and verification are handled by the authentication service

foreignFields.name: member_id
foreignFields.description: Member account's {@link hrms_members.id}.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Unique verification token (hash of email + random salt).

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Token expiration timestamp after which verification is invalid.

plainFields.name: used_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the token was used to verify the email address. Null if token is unused.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Record creation timestamp.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Record last update timestamp.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Record deletion timestamp for soft delete (used tokens are soft deleted).

models.name: hrms_guests
models.description:
Temporary guest accounts for unauthenticated visitors, identified by device fingerprint.

Guest accounts represent temporary visitor sessions that do not have authentication credentials (email/password). Each guest account is uniquely identified by a device fingerprint, which combines browser/device characteristics to maintain session continuity across requests.

Key characteristics:
- Temporary accounts that exist for the duration of a visitor session
- No email or password authentication required
- Identified by device fingerprint for session persistence
- Can be soft-deleted when the session expires or is cleared
- Sessions are stored in the separate {@link hrms_guest_sessions} table

This table serves as the canonical identity record for guest actors in the system, with one-to-many relationships to session tokens. Guest accounts are typically short-lived and are automatically cleaned up when sessions expire.

plainFields.name: device_fingerprint
plainFields.description: Unique device fingerprint that identifies this guest account. Generated by combining browser characteristics (user agent, screen resolution, timezone, etc.) to create a persistent identifier for the device.

plainFields.name: ip_address
plainFields.description: IP address of the guest's last known location. Used for security and session tracking.

plainFields.name: user_agent
plainFields.description: Browser user agent string from the last request. Helps identify device/browser characteristics.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this guest account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this guest account was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this guest account was soft-deleted. NULL means active.

models.name: hrms_guest_sessions
models.description:
Temporary session tokens for guest access with device-based identification.

Each guest session is identified by a UUID and stores connection metadata including IP address, browser referrer information, and expiration timestamp. Sessions are append-only audit records that track when guests access the system with their device fingerprint.

This table is a child of the {@link hrms_guests} actor table and supports the guest actor's session pattern. Sessions expire automatically based on security requirements and cannot be edited directly.

Related entities:
- Parent: {@link hrms_guests} - Guest account with device fingerprint
- Session management is handled through authentication flows, not direct CRUD operations

foreignFields.name: hrms_guest_id
foreignFields.description: Guest account's {@link hrms_guests.id}. Identifies which guest this session belongs to.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address of the device that created this session.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Browser referrer URL or landing page that initiated the session.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Full referrer header information from the browser request.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this session was created.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Expiration timestamp for this session. Sessions are temporary and must expire for security.

models.name: hrms_activity_logs
models.description:
Centralized audit trail capturing all significant system actions per organization.

This table serves as the system-wide event log for compliance and debugging. Each entry records an action performed by a user within an organization context, including:

- Employee lifecycle events: invited, deactivated, reactivated
- Contract events: created, edited
- Project events: created, archived, completed, deleted
- Task events: status changed
- Timesheet events: submitted, approved, rejected
- Role events: assigned, changed

Users with org:manage permission can view the full activity log for their organization.

{@link hrms_organizations} - Each log entry belongs to exactly one organization.
{@link hrms_members} - Records which user performed the action.
{@link hrms_employees} - Referenced for employee-related actions.
{@link hrms_projects} - Referenced for project-related actions.
{@link hrms_tasks} - Referenced for task-related actions.
{@link hrms_timesheets} - Referenced for timesheet-related actions.
{@link hrms_organization_roles} - Referenced for role-related actions.

foreignFields.name: organization_id
foreignFields.description: Organization that this activity belongs to. {@link hrms_organizations.id}

foreignFields.name: performed_by_id
foreignFields.description: User who performed the action. {@link hrms_members.id}

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description: Type of action performed. Values: 'employee.invited', 'employee.deactivated', 'employee.reactivated', 'contract.created', 'contract.edited', 'project.created', 'project.archived', 'project.completed', 'project.deleted', 'task.status_changed', 'timesheet.submitted', 'timesheet.approved', 'timesheet.rejected', 'role.assigned', 'role.changed'.

plainFields.name: target_entity
plainFields.description: Type of entity that was affected. Values: 'employee', 'contract', 'project', 'task', 'timesheet', 'role', 'user'.

plainFields.name: target_id
plainFields.description: ID of the target entity (nullable if action doesn't target a specific entity).

plainFields.name: details
plainFields.description: Additional details about the action (e.g., field changes, reasons).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the action was performed.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp (nullable means not deleted).

models.name: hrms_organizations
models.description:
Multi-tenant organization entities with settings and owner reference.

Organizations represent independent tenants in the system, each with its own employees, projects, tasks, and data. Organizations are created by users during initial sign-up and operate as isolated units with organization-specific settings including currency, timezone, and fiscal calendar.

Organizations are owned by a single user (organization owner) who has full control over organization settings, member management, and role configuration. Owners can delete organizations only when all pending timesheets are resolved and no active employee contracts exist. When an organization is deleted, all associated employees, projects, tasks, timelogs, and timesheets are permanently deleted, but the owner's account remains (unassociated with any organization).

Related entities: {@link hrms_organization_members}, {@link hrms_organization_roles}, {@link hrms_employees}, {@link hrms_projects}

foreignFields.name: owner_id
foreignFields.description: Organization owner's member account reference. The owner has full control over organization settings and member management.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Organization display name. Must be unique across all organizations.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional organization description.

plainFields.name: logo_uri
plainFields.description: Organization logo image URL.

plainFields.name: currency
plainFields.description: Organization currency code (e.g., USD, EUR, KRW).

plainFields.name: timezone
plainFields.description: Organization timezone (e.g., Asia/Seoul, America/New_York).

plainFields.name: fiscal_start_month
plainFields.description: Fiscal year start month (1-12, where 1=January).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Organization creation timestamp.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Organization last update timestamp.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Organization soft delete timestamp (null if not deleted).

models.name: hrms_organization_members
models.description:
Links users (members) to organizations with role assignment, supporting multi-organization membership.

Each organization member represents a user's participation in a specific organization with an assigned role. Users can belong to multiple organizations, each with potentially different roles and permissions.

Key relationships:
- {@link hrms_members} — The user account this membership belongs to
- {@link hrms_organizations} — The organization this membership is for
- {@link hrms_organization_roles} — The role assigned within this organization

Business rules:
- A member can only have one membership per organization (enforced by unique constraint)
- Role determines the permissions and access level within the organization
- Deactivated employees are still linked via this table but with status flag in hrms_employees

foreignFields.name: hrms_member_id
foreignFields.description: Member's {@link hrms_members.id}. The user account this organization membership belongs to.

foreignFields.name: hrms_organization_id
foreignFields.description: Organization's {@link hrms_organizations.id}. The organization this membership is for.

foreignFields.name: hrms_organization_role_id
foreignFields.description: Role's {@link hrms_organization_roles.id}. The role assigned to this member within the organization.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Record creation timestamp.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Record last update timestamp.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. Null means active, non-null means deleted.

models.name: hrms_organization_roles
models.description:
Custom role definitions within each organization, including built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee) and user-created custom roles.

Each organization maintains its own set of roles with permission sets. Organization owners can create, edit, and delete custom roles. Built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee) cannot be deleted. Each organization member is assigned exactly one role from this organization's role set.

This table supports the multi-tenancy architecture where permissions and roles are organization-specific. Related entities include {@link hrms_organization_members} (which references roles), {@link hrms_organizations} (parent organization), and {@link hrms_organization_role_permissions} (normalized permission storage).

foreignFields.name: organization_id
foreignFields.description: Belonging organization's {@link hrms_organizations.id}. Each organization has its own independent set of roles.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Role name (e.g., Owner, Manager, Employee, or custom name). Must be unique within the organization.

plainFields.name: is_builtin
plainFields.description: Whether this is a built-in role (Owner, Manager, Employee) that cannot be deleted. Custom roles have this set to false.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Role creation timestamp.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last role update timestamp.

models.name: hrms_organization_role_permissions
models.description:
Normalized storage of role permissions for 1NF compliance.

Stores one permission code per row (e.g., "employee:manage", "time:approve") to avoid storing arrays or JSON in the role table. Each role can have multiple permissions, enabling flexible permission sets per custom role.

**Relationships**:
- Belongs to a single {@link hrms_organization_roles} - each permission is associated with exactly one role
- Permissions are managed exclusively through the role entity, not independently

**Data Integrity**:
- Unique constraint prevents duplicate permissions for the same role
- All permission codes follow the format "category:action" (e.g., "org:manage", "employee:view")

foreignFields.name: hrms_organization_role_id
foreignFields.description: Role's {@link hrms_organization_roles.id}. Each permission belongs to exactly one role.

plainFields.name: permission
plainFields.description: Permission code following the format "category:action" (e.g., "org:manage", "employee:view", "time:approve", "project:manage", "report:view"). Defines a specific action a role can perform.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this permission record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this permission record was last updated.

models.name: hrms_employees
models.description:
Employee records linking user accounts to organizational roles, departments, and employment details.

This table represents employees within the multi-tenant organization system. Each employee record connects to an organization member record, establishing the relationship between a user and their role within a specific organization. Employees have employment-specific attributes including department assignment, position title, and employment type classification.

Key relationships:
- Each employee belongs to exactly one organization member record ({@link hrms_organization_members.id})
- Each employee has one role assignment within their organization ({@link hrms_organization_roles.id})
- Employees may belong to an optional department ({@link hrms_departments.id})
- Employees can have multiple historical contracts ({@link hrms_employee_contracts})
- Employees can create timelogs ({@link hrms_timelogs}) and timesheets ({@link hrms_timesheets})

The employee record serves as the core employment entity, separate from the authentication user account. This allows the system to track employment history, contracts, and organizational role assignments independently of user login credentials.

foreignFields.name: organization_member_id
foreignFields.description: Organization member record that connects this employee to a user account and organization. {@link hrms_organization_members.id}.

foreignFields.name: role_id
foreignFields.description: Role assigned to this employee within the organization. Determines permissions and access levels. {@link hrms_organization_roles.id}.

foreignFields.name: department_id
foreignFields.description: Optional department assignment for organizational structure. {@link hrms_departments.id}.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: Display name for the employee, separate from the user's global profile name.

plainFields.name: position
plainFields.description: Job title or position within the organization (e.g., Senior Developer, Marketing Manager).

plainFields.name: employment_type
plainFields.description: Employment classification: full-time, part-time, contractor, intern.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Employment status: active or deactivated. Deactivated employees cannot log time or submit timesheets.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Record creation timestamp.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Record last update timestamp.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. NULL means record is active.

models.name: hrms_employee_contracts
models.description:
Historical employment contract records that track the terms of employment for employees over time.

This table stores contract history for each employee, including pay rate, pay period, working hours, and contract dates. At any given time, only one contract can be active for an employee. When a new contract is created, the previous active contract is automatically terminated.

**Key Features**:

- Historical record of employment terms with immutable past contracts
- One-to-many relationship with {@link hrms_employees} (one employee, many contracts)
- Active contract tracking through date ranges (start_date, end_date)
- Pay rate and pay period configuration for compensation tracking
- Working hours per week specification for time tracking calculations

**Business Rules**:

- Only one contract can be active at a time per employee
- Creating a new contract automatically ends the previous active contract
- Past contracts are immutable and cannot be edited
- Employees can view their own contracts
- Users with `employee:view` permission can view any employee's contracts

foreignFields.name: hrms_employee_id
foreignFields.description: Employee's {@link hrms_employees.id}. Belongs to one employee who may have multiple contracts over time.

plainFields.name: start_date
plainFields.description: Contract start date and time. Required for all contracts.

plainFields.name: end_date
plainFields.description: Contract end date and time. Nullable for ongoing contracts without an end date.

plainFields.name: pay_rate
plainFields.description: Pay rate numeric value. Required for compensation tracking.

plainFields.name: pay_period
plainFields.description: Pay period classification: hourly, daily, weekly, or monthly.

plainFields.name: working_hours_per_week
plainFields.description: Working hours per week specification, e.g., 40 for full-time. Required for time tracking calculations.

plainFields.name: notes
plainFields.description: Optional notes or additional contract terms. Can be null.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Record creation timestamp.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Record last update timestamp.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. Nullable for undeleted records.

models.name: hrms_departments
models.description:
Organizational department units with parent-child hierarchy support within each organization.

Departments represent the organizational structure of an organization, allowing departments to be organized in a hierarchy with optional parent-child relationships (one level of nesting). Each department belongs to exactly one organization and can have an optional parent department, creating a two-level organizational chart.

Key relationships:
- Belongs to {@link hrms_organizations} via organization_id
- Parent-department relationship via parent_id (self-referencing FK)
- Employees reference this table via hrms_employees.department_id

Behavioral notes:
- When a department is deleted, all employee records in that department have their department_id set to NULL
- Department names must be unique within each organization
- Supports soft delete via deleted_at for audit purposes

foreignFields.name: organization_id
foreignFields.description: Organization this department belongs to. {@link hrms_organizations.id}

foreignFields.name: parent_id
foreignFields.description: Parent department for hierarchy (one level nesting). {@link hrms_departments.id}

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Department name. Must be unique within the organization.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional department description or details.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the department was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the department was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the department was soft deleted (nullable = not deleted).

models.name: hrms_projects
models.description: Work initiatives that employees track time against. Projects organize work with budget tracking, date ranges, and status management. Each project belongs to an organization and can have multiple tasks, project members, and associated timelogs. Archived or completed projects cannot receive new timelog entries but preserve historical data. Project status transitions control workflow: active projects accept time entries, while archived/completed projects are closed to new work. Organization owners and project managers can create, edit, archive, complete, and delete projects (with timelog constraints).

foreignFields.name: hrms_organization_id
foreignFields.description: Belonging organization's {@link hrms_organizations.id}. Organization provides multi-tenancy isolation for all project data.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Project name. Required for identification and display in project lists and task assignments.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional project description with details about scope, objectives, and deliverables.

plainFields.name: color_code
plainFields.description: Hex color code (e.g., #3498db) for UI display and project visualization. Required for color-coded project boards and timers.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Project status: 'active' (accepting time entries), 'archived' (closed, preserved), 'completed' (finished work). Active projects allow new timelogs; archived/completed projects preserve historical data only.

plainFields.name: budget_hours
plainFields.description: Total estimated hours for the project. Used for budget tracking and utilization reporting. Projects without budget are excluded from budget reports.

plainFields.name: start_date
plainFields.description: Optional project start date for timeline planning and reporting.

plainFields.name: end_date
plainFields.description: Optional project end date for timeline planning and reporting.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Creation timestamp when the project was first created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update timestamp for the project record.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. When present, project is marked as deleted but preserved for audit purposes.

models.name: hrms_project_members
models.description:
Employee-project membership assignments that link employees to projects with role designation.

This table tracks which employees are assigned to which projects and their role within that project (member or project-lead). Each membership represents a one-to-one relationship between an employee and a project - an employee can have multiple project memberships across different projects, but only one membership per project.

Project leads can manage tasks within their project, while regular members can view and work on tasks. Users with `project:manage` permission can assign employees to projects, change their roles, or remove them entirely.

**Key Relationships**:
- Belongs to {@link hrms_employees} - The employee who is a member of the project
- Belongs to {@link hrms_projects} - The project that includes this employee as a member

**Status Management**:
- Active memberships allow the employee to work on the project
- Inactive memberships preserve historical assignment data without active participation
- Memberships can be reactivated by users with `project:manage` permission

foreignFields.name: employee_id
foreignFields.description: Employee's {@link hrms_employees.id}. The employee who is assigned to this project.

foreignFields.name: project_id
foreignFields.description: Project's {@link hrms_projects.id}. The project that this employee is a member of.

plainFields.name: role
plainFields.description: Role within the project: 'member' or 'project-lead'. Project leads can manage tasks within their project, while members can view and work on tasks.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Membership status: 'active' or 'inactive'. Active memberships allow the employee to work on the project. Inactive memberships preserve historical data without active participation.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this membership was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this membership was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this membership was soft-deleted (optional).

models.name: hrms_tasks
models.description:
Work items within projects that employees track time against. Tasks support optional parent-child hierarchy for subtasks and track status through a workflow (open → in-progress → completed → closed).

Tasks are independently managed by users with project:manage permission - they can create, search, filter, and delete tasks regardless of project context. Each task belongs to exactly one project and may be assigned to an employee. Tasks have estimated hours, due dates, priority levels, and a billable flag for time tracking purposes.

Related entities:
- {@link hrms_projects} - Each task belongs to exactly one project
- {@link hrms_employees} - Optional assignment to an employee (must be a project member)
- {@link hrms_task_status_histories} - Audit trail of status changes (managed in same component but generated separately)

foreignFields.name: hrms_project_id
foreignFields.description: Project that this task belongs to. {@link hrms_projects.id}

foreignFields.name: hrms_employee_id
foreignFields.description: Employee assigned to this task. {@link hrms_employees.id}

foreignFields.name: hrms_task_id
foreignFields.description: Parent task for subtasks. {@link hrms_tasks.id}

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Task title. Required field for task identification.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Task description with optional details about the work item.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Task status: open, in-progress, completed, or closed.

plainFields.name: priority
plainFields.description: Task priority level: low, medium, high, or urgent.

plainFields.name: estimated_hours
plainFields.description: Estimated hours required to complete the task.

plainFields.name: due_date
plainFields.description: Optional due date for task completion.

plainFields.name: billable
plainFields.description: Whether this task time is billable to client.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the task was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the task was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the task was soft-deleted.

models.name: hrms_task_status_histories
models.description:
Audit trail table that captures all status changes made to tasks in the system. This is a snapshot table that records point-in-time status transitions for compliance and historical tracking purposes.

Each entry represents a single status change event, capturing the previous status (old_status), the new status (new_status), the timestamp of the change, and the user (member) who initiated the change. This enables complete auditability of task lifecycle and allows reconstruction of task history.

Relationships:
- Belongs to a {@link hrms_tasks} task that had its status changed
- Performed by a {@link hrms_members} user who has project management permissions

This table is append-only and read-only from the user perspective. Status history is automatically created by the system when task status is modified through the project management workflow.

foreignFields.name: hrms_task_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the {@link hrms_tasks.id} that had its status changed.

foreignFields.name: hrms_member_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the {@link hrms_members.id} who made the status change.

plainFields.name: old_status
plainFields.description: The previous status value before the change (open, in-progress, completed, closed).

plainFields.name: new_status
plainFields.description: The new status value after the change (open, in-progress, completed, closed).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the status change occurred.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update timestamp for soft delete tracking.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp (nullable, null means active).

models.name: hrms_timelogs
models.description:
Individual time entries that employees create to track work done on projects and tasks.

This is a primary business entity representing discrete time logged by employees. Each timelog records the date worked, duration in minutes, which project and task (if any) the time was spent on, a description of work performed, and whether the time is billable to clients.

Timelogs can only be created for projects the employee is assigned to. Employees can manage their own timelogs (edit/delete only if not in an approved timesheet). Users with the `time:manage` permission can modify any employee's timelogs. Timelogs are automatically included in weekly timesheets and become locked once those timesheets are approved.

**Key relationships**:
- Belongs to a single employee (`{@link hrms_employees}`) who logged the time
- Belongs to a single project (`{@link hrms_projects}`) the time was spent on
- Optionally belongs to a task (`{@link hrms_tasks}`) within that project
- Referenced by timesheets (`{@link hrms_timesheets}`) which group timelogs by week

**Business rules**:
- Employees can only create timelogs for themselves
- Employees can only edit/delete their own timelogs that are not in submitted or approved timesheets
- Project and task must belong to a project the employee is assigned to
- Duration is stored in minutes for precise time tracking

foreignFields.name: employee_id
foreignFields.description: Employee who logged this time. {@link hrms_employees.id}

foreignFields.name: project_id
foreignFields.description: Project this time was spent on. {@link hrms_projects.id}

foreignFields.name: task_id
foreignFields.description: Optional task within the project this time was spent on. {@link hrms_tasks.id}

plainFields.name: billable
plainFields.description: Whether this time is billable to clients. Default is true.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When this timelog was created.

plainFields.name: date
plainFields.description: The date this work was performed (stored as datetime at midnight).

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Description of what work was performed during this time entry.

plainFields.name: duration_minutes
plainFields.description: Duration of this time entry in minutes.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: When this timelog was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. NULL means the record is active.

models.name: hrms_timesheets
models.description:
Weekly collections of timelogs with approval workflow for employee timesheet management.

A timesheet represents all timelogs for a specific employee within a calendar week (Monday to Sunday). Timesheets follow an approval workflow with states: draft (editable), submitted (pending approval), approved (locked and final), or rejected (return to draft with reason).

Key relationships:
- Belongs to {@link hrms_employees} - Each timesheet is owned by a single employee who logs time against it
- Reviewed by {@link hrms_members} - Managers or approvers (member accounts) who approve or reject timesheets

Business rules:
- Only the owning employee can create and edit draft timesheets
- A timesheet cannot be submitted if it has no timelogs
- Each employee can have only one submitted or approved timesheet per week
- Approved timesheets lock all included timelogs (cannot be edited or deleted)
- Rejected timesheets include a rejection reason and return to draft status

This table enables the weekly timesheet approval workflow central to the time tracking system.

foreignFields.name: hrms_employee_id
foreignFields.description: Employee who owns this timesheet and logged the time entries. {@link hrms_employees.id}

foreignFields.name: reviewed_by
foreignFields.description: Member (manager/approver) who approved or rejected this timesheet. {@link hrms_members.id}

plainFields.name: week_start_date
plainFields.description: The Monday start date of the week covered by this timesheet. Timesheets are always organized by calendar weeks (Monday to Sunday).

plainFields.name: week_end_date
plainFields.description: The Sunday end date of the week covered by this timesheet. Calculated as week_start_date + 6 days.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Approval workflow status of the timesheet: draft (editable), submitted (pending approval), approved (locked and final), rejected (returned to draft with reason).

plainFields.name: total_hours
plainFields.description: Total hours logged in this timesheet, calculated as the sum of durations from all associated timelogs. Stored as a denormalized value for reporting efficiency.

plainFields.name: submitted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the employee submitted this timesheet for approval. Null for draft timesheets.

plainFields.name: reviewed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the timesheet was approved or rejected by an approver. Null for draft and submitted timesheets.

plainFields.name: rejection_reason
plainFields.description: Reason for rejection provided by the approver. Required when status is rejected, null otherwise.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Creation timestamp of this timesheet record.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update timestamp of this timesheet record.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp. Null if the timesheet is not deleted.

models.name: hrms_timers
models.description:
Live timer tracking sessions for real-time employee time tracking.

Employees can start a timer to track time in real-time. Each employee can have at most one active timer at a time. Starting a timer requires selecting a project and optionally a task. When the timer is stopped, it automatically creates a timelog entry with the calculated duration. Employees can also discard their timer without creating a timelog.

Key relationships:
- Belongs to a single {@link hrms_employees} employee (owner)
- References a {@link hrms_projects} project (required) - the project being tracked against
- Optionally references a {@link hrms_tasks} task within the selected project
- Many timers can be stopped and converted to {@link hrms_timelogs} over the employee's lifetime

foreignFields.name: hrms_employee_id
foreignFields.description: Employee owner of this timer. {@link hrms_employees.id}

foreignFields.name: hrms_project_id
foreignFields.description: Project being tracked. {@link hrms_projects.id}

foreignFields.name: hrms_task_id
foreignFields.description: Optional task being tracked. {@link hrms_tasks.id}

plainFields.name: start_at
plainFields.description: Timer start timestamp when the timer was started.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional description of what the employee is working on during this timer session.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Record creation timestamp.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Record last update timestamp.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp (NULL means active, not deleted).

models.name: hrms_files
models.description:
File metadata for organization logos, user avatars, and document attachments with storage path and organization context.

This table serves as the central repository for all uploaded files in the system, including organization logos, user profile avatars, and document attachments. Files are associated with organizations for multi-tenancy isolation and can be owned by different entity types (organizations or members) through polymorphic ownership.

The table supports the complete file upload workflow from temporary validation to permanent storage. Each file record includes validation status tracking, MIME type detection, and size constraints to ensure data integrity and security. Files are soft-deleted to preserve historical references while marking them as inaccessible.

foreignFields.name: organization_id
foreignFields.description: The organization that owns this file. All files are scoped to their parent organization for multi-tenancy isolation.

foreignFields.name: owner_id
foreignFields.description: Polymorphic owner reference for files. When owner_type is 'member', references a user's profile avatar via {@link hrms_members.id}. When null, the file belongs to the organization directly (e.g., organization logo, shared documents).

plainFields.name: filename
plainFields.description: Original filename as uploaded by the user, preserved for display purposes.

plainFields.name: storage_path
plainFields.description: Internal storage path or URL where the file content is stored, used for retrieval.

plainFields.name: mime_type
plainFields.description: MIME type of the file detected during upload (e.g., image/jpeg, application/pdf).

plainFields.name: file_size
plainFields.description: File size in bytes, recorded at upload time.

plainFields.name: file_category
plainFields.description: Category classification: 'organization_logo' for org logos, 'user_avatar' for profile pictures, 'document' for general attachments.

plainFields.name: owner_type
plainFields.description: Type of owner for polymorphic association: 'member' for user avatars, null for organization-owned files.

plainFields.name: validation_status
plainFields.description: Current validation status: 'pending' (awaiting virus scan), 'validated' (passed security checks), 'rejected' (failed validation).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the file was created and initially stored.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the file record was last updated with new metadata.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. When null, file is active. When set, file is marked for deletion but retained for historical references.

models.name: hrms_file_uploads
models.description:
Tracks the file upload workflow from temporary storage to permanent storage, including validation status and ownership assignment.

This table supports the file upload process by maintaining:
- Original filename and upload metadata
- Temporary and permanent storage paths
- Upload state (pending, validating, completed, failed)
- Error tracking for failed uploads

When a file is uploaded:
1. A record is created with pending state
2. File is scanned and validated
3. Upon success, file metadata is stored in hrms_files and upload record is updated to completed
4. If validation fails, upload state is set to failed with error message

Referenced by:
- {@link hrms_files} - The uploaded file's permanent metadata
- {@link hrms_organizations} - Organization context for the upload
- {@link hrms_members} - Member who initiated the upload

foreignFields.name: organization_id
foreignFields.description: Organization context for the file upload. {@link hrms_organizations.id}

foreignFields.name: member_id
foreignFields.description: Member who initiated the file upload. {@link hrms_members.id}

foreignFields.name: file_id
foreignFields.description: The uploaded file's permanent metadata after successful validation. {@link hrms_files.id}

plainFields.name: original_filename
plainFields.description: Original filename provided by the user during upload.

plainFields.name: file_type
plainFields.description: MIME type of the uploaded file (e.g., image/png, application/pdf).

plainFields.name: file_size
plainFields.description: File size in bytes.

plainFields.name: validation_status
plainFields.description: Validation result: pending, valid, invalid. Used for virus scanning and content validation.

plainFields.name: temporary_storage_path
plainFields.description: Path to temporary storage location before permanent storage is assigned.

plainFields.name: permanent_storage_path
plainFields.description: Path to permanent storage location after successful upload and validation.

plainFields.name: upload_state
plainFields.description: Current upload workflow state: pending, validating, completed, failed.

plainFields.name: error_message
plainFields.description: Error description if upload or validation failed.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Upload request timestamp.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update timestamp.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp.
